Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the EnergiCore Utilities Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to EnergiCore Utilities' Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Kline, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; and Mike Thompson, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1.  Strong operational performance in our generation fleet.
    2.  Continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio.
    3.  Effective cost management.
    4.  Progress on our infrastructure investments.

Let me provide some more detail on these four key aspects.

Starting with our strong operational performance across the generation fleet. Our Q3 consolidated adjusted EBITDA reached $1.28 billion, marking a 14% increase from $1.12 billion in Q3 2023 and an 8% sequential rise from $1.18 billion in Q2 2024. This strong showing supported adjusted EPS of $1.42, up 18% year-over-year from $1.20 and 7% higher than Q2's $1.33. Total revenue hit $4.75 billion, reflecting 11% growth from $4.28 billion last year, thanks to elevated power prices in competitive markets, expansion in our regulated rate base, and output from expanding renewables. Net income for common shareholders stood at $850 million, or $1.15 per diluted share, compared to $720 million or $0.98 per share a year ago.

Breaking it down by segments, our Regulated Utilities operations—covering transmission and distribution in PJM, MISO, and SPP for 12 million customers—delivered $825 million in adjusted EBITDA, a 12% YoY gain from $735 million and steady sequentially. Rate base expanded to $42.5 billion, up 9% year-over-year, powered by $3.2 billion in capex including $1.1 billion for grid hardening informed by past events like Hurricane Ida and $800 million for advanced metering infrastructure. We maintained a solid 10.8% ROE, aided by favorable FERC formula rate adjustments in PJM and approved riders for wildfire mitigation in MISO.

Load grew 4% on a weather-normalized basis, driven by industrial electrification in the Midwest tied to data center deals similar to Meta's large PJM agreements, plus residential EV uptake reaching 2.5% penetration. AFUDC equity climbed 15% to $180 million, helping counter regulatory lag. O&M costs increased 6% from storm recovery but were partly offset by efficiencies from our Oracle CC&B ERP system.

In Competitive Generation, we hit a record $455 million adjusted EBITDA, surging 22% YoY from $375 million and 18% from Q2's $385 million. Our 28 GW fleet—45% renewables, 35% efficient combined-cycle gas, 15% nuclear, 5% peakers—posted a blended 68% capacity factor, improved from 62% last year, due to smart dispatch in ERCOT and ISO-NE.

Renewables led with our 8.5 GW portfolio (55% wind, 35% solar, 10% storage) generating $210 million EBITDA, up 25% YoY with 18% higher production on resource adequacy gains. Key wins included full commercial operation of the 450 MW Rattlesnake Solar plus 200 MW/800 MWh BESS hybrid in ERCOT under a 12-year PPA with a top Fortune 100 buyer at over 12% IRR, and repowers at our 600 MW Plains Wind farms using advanced longer blades and drivetrains like Vestas' newest platforms, lifting capacity factors 15%.

Thermal generation added $180 million, up 15% YoY despite Henry Hub gas at $2.85/MMBtu versus $2.60 last year. CCGT heat rates improved 2% to 7,200 Btu/kWh, and we cleared 2.5 GW in PJM's recent BRA auction at $300/MW-day, outperforming the clearing price by 20%. Nuclear at 2.2 GW achieved 93% uptime following steam generator upgrades akin to Vogtle.

By region, ERCOT excelled with 25% segment EBITDA growth amid summer peaks over 85 GW from crypto and AI data centers. PJM saw softer spark spreads from mild weather but gained $45 million from 500 MW demand response. SPP navigated coal retirements with our 1.2 GW gas peakers capturing scarcity during heat events. Corporate items included $25 million from IRA Section 45X tax credits on BESS domestic content and $15 million in Winter Storm Uri insurance recoveries. Interest expense rose 10% to $320 million on $18 billion debt, but all-in cost stays at 4.2% with 75% fixed.

For full-year 2024, we're affirming adjusted EBITDA of $4.75 to $4.85 billion, adjusted EPS of $5.40 to $5.60, and capex at $5.2 billion. Q4 EBITDA eyes $1.15 to $1.25 billion, balancing seasonal hydro softness with holiday loads and capacity payments. For 2025, expect adjusted EBITDA of $5.2 to $5.5 billion, up 9-14%, from 1.2 GW renewables COD including 600 MW offshore wind, rate base to $46 billion, and 5% load growth via 3 GW hyperscaler PPAs. EPS of $5.80 to $6.20 factors 20 bps rate pressure offset by 15% FCF growth to $2.3 billion, backing our 4.2% dividend and $1.5 billion buyback.

Risks encompass gas volatility—with 70% Henry Hub hedges at $3.00 to $3.20—and potential PJM FERC ROE challenges, tempered by our 10 GW interconnection queue. Tailwinds include DOE grid funding and EIA's doubled power demand forecast by 2030 from AI.

Next, on continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio. As we push forward with our long-term strategy, we're making major investments in renewables and the clean energy transition, central to EnergiCore Utilities' growth. With surging demand from electrification, data centers, and EVs, we're evolving from baseload reliability to low-carbon leadership. In Q3 2024, renewables claim 45% of our FY2024 capex budget, up from 32% in 2021. We're investing $2.8 billion this year in greenfield and brownfield efforts: $1.2 billion in utility-scale solar, $900 million in onshore and offshore wind, $500 million in battery storage systems, and $200 million in long-duration storage and green hydrogen pilots. For FY2025, this rises to $3.5 billion, over 50% of capex, financed 60% by regulated utility cash flows, 30% green bonds at 3.8% yield leveraging strong S&P and Moody's ESG scores, and 10% tax equity.

Our renewable pipeline totals 12.5 GW through 2028, with 4.2 GW building and 8.3 GW advancing. Year-to-date, we synced 850 MW solar PV in ERCOT using First Solar Series 7 bifacial modules at 22.6% efficiency and $28/MWh LCOE, down 15% YoY from polysilicon drops and IRA manufacturing credits. In SPP, 450 MW onshore Vestas V150-4.2 MW turbines with 112-meter rotors for low winds went live. Offshore, our 50% Atlantic Horizon 800 MW stake—scaled like Vineyard Wind—tracks for H2 2026 COD with GE Vernova Haliade-X 14 MW units.

In storage, 1.2 GWh deployed across four sites, including a 400 MWh/100 MW four-hour PJM system hybridized with combustion turbines using CATL LFP cells at 95% efficiency and Fluence AI management for <1% annual degradation. We aim for 20% CAGR in storage to 2030 via FERC 2222 for DER markets.

Clean fuels advance with $150 million green hydrogen at repurposed Mystic CT in ISO-NE, Phase 1 at 10 tonnes/day from 20 MW ITM Power electrolyzers on curtailed renewables, tying to DOE Hubs. LCOH at $3.50/kg rivals SMR gray post-45V PTC.

Tailored regionally: ERCOT's 10% load growth from data centers secured 1.5 GW solar-storage PPAs with AWS at $35/MWh, 12-14% IRR. CAISO's 600 MW Imperial Valley solar with agrivoltaics hits LADWP RPS. MISO's 200 GW queue de-risked 2 GW via reconductoring with 3M composites. Our 20% North Sea Dogger Bank JV adds 300 MW at UK CfD £41.61/MWh.

These yield 10-12% ROE above hurdle, boosted by IRA 30-50% ITC/PTC, RECs at $5-8/MWh from Microsoft/Google markets. 85% of 2025-2027 output PPAs locked, 70% IG counterparties, shielding ERCOT negatives to -$200/MWh.

Trends favor: BNEF $1.1T global renewables capex by 2025, 40 GW US annual adds, 35 GW data center load by 2030 at $50/MWh premium. Costs down: solar 89%, wind 70%, BESS 89% since 2010 per Lazard. We counter 5-year PJM/MISO queues with $300M grid contributions, pushing FERC reforms.

This drives 8-10% EPS growth, renewables to 55% fleet by 2030 from 28%, 60% carbon cut ahead of SEC rules. Value over greenwashing, trading 18x P/E discount to NextEra peers.

Third, our effective cost management. Our rate base growth outlook and key assumptions form a key part of controlling costs while expanding. As a multi-state regulated utility serving over 10 million customers in PJM, MISO, and SPP, rate base ended Q3 at $42.5 billion, up 7.2% YoY. We target 6.5-7.0% CAGR through 2028, reaching $65-70 billion, fueling 8-10% EPS growth and strong returns amid electrification.

This rests on a $22 billion five-year capex plan—$4.4 billion yearly average—55% T&D, 30% generation/renewables, 10% customer/grid modernization, rest environmental/reliability, up 12% prior plan for regulation and inflation.

T&D anchors with $12.1 billion, including $3.2 billion transmission like 500 kV reconductoring in Ohio/Pennsylvania akin to FirstEnergy. Earning 10.15% ROE plus AFUDC for 50-75 bps EPS yearly. Flagship $450 million Mid-Atlantic Resilience Line, FERC-approved 345 kV upgrade for PATH, 2026 in-service, unlocking 1.2 GW for AWS/Microsoft data centers driving 4-5% peaks.

Generation $6.6 billion for net-zero 2045: renewables 35% capex share, up from 20%, IRA PTC/ITC. 2.5 GW solar-storage: 600 MW Prairie Sun Illinois MISO with NextEra EPC, 400 MW Desert Bloom Texas SPP with 200 MWh Fluence LFP, $25-30/MWh LCOE, 30-50% ITC Energy Communities. $1.8 billion gas peakers like two 200 MW H-class Georgia for intermittency, 12-14% IRR.

$2.2 billion grid mod: AMI for 2M meters by 2027 like Dominion, DERMS for 1 GW customer solar, adding 1-1.5% non-capex growth via O&M normalization.

Regionally: PJM Northeast (PA/OH/NJ, 45% rate base) 7.5% CAGR from 6% EV/industrial load, PUCN $1.2B T&D rider 55% equity AFUDC vs. inflation. MISO Midwest (IL/MI, 30%) 6% CAGR, wind repowers/CCUS Edwards Unit 45Q $85/ton, LRTP $600M HR. SPP Southwest (TX/OK, 25%) 8% CAGR, ERCOT-adjacent, 300 MW BESS queue, Texas PBR 70% sharing.

Assumptions: 2.5-3% load CAGR, peaks +5%; 90% rate base placement 12 months, 9.75-10.5% ROE, two rate cases/jurisdiction 75 bps bumps, PJM formula 85% T&D. 3-4% inflation offset 15% efficiencies Siemens/First Solar PPAs; Fed 3.5-4.5%, 100 bps rise -20 bps growth. Gas $3.50 80% hedge, 1.2 GW coal retire offset 1 GW CCGT, auctions $100-120/kW-yr net long 500 MW. IRA $1.2B NPV, IIJA $300M; risks IRA repeal -10% EPS, FERC 1920 delay.

De-risk via Orsted offshore JVs, coal-renewables swaps $400M, $150M Grid Zero 2% O&M savings.

This resilient growth outperforms peers like Entergy/Ameren, 60% early AFUDC-funded.

Finally, progress on infrastructure investments. Just to note on forward-looking aspects, statements here reflect current views on operations, performance, and markets. Results could vary from regulatory shifts, commodity swings, supply chains, weather, cyber, demand from electrification/decarb. See 10-K/10-Q risks; no update duty except law.

For FY2025+, reaffirm adjusted EPS $5.40-$5.70 midpoint 7% over 2024 $5.50-ish, from 6.5% rate base growth via $2.8-3.2B capex on hardening, renewables, thermal mods. AFUDC adds 15 cents EPS vs. 12 cents 2024.

Revenues $12.5-13.2B, +4-8%, 2.5-3% load from 1.2 GW AWS/Google data centers ERCOT/PJM, EV to 15% CA/TX by 2027. Wholesale +7% to $1.8B on ISO-NE/MISO spark, gas $3.50-4.00 NYMEX, 12GW gas 7,200 Btu/kWh.

Ops: 1.8 GW renewables 2025—1.2 GW First Solar bifacial 22%+, 600 MW 4-hr BESS like ERCOT Fluence—42% renewables of 35 GW, $450M IRA PTC/ITC direct pay. Post-2025 2.5 GW incl. Orsted-like offshore Northeast $120/kW-month auctions.

Texas 40% EBITDA, ERCOT 85 GW winter peaks vs. 5.2 GW, 4.1% demand vs. 2.8% national, $450M battery peakers NERC blackstart post-Uri. CA CPUC NEM 3.0 caps DG but 2.1 GW CCAs hedge 85% RPS PPAs Orsted/Clearway $45/MWh to 2030.

Fuel-agnostic: $1.2B Advanced Grid AI DERMS AutoGrid 15 GW load $200M LMP uplift; nuclear 2.4 GW extensions Entergy Palisades-style Diablo dry cask 20 yrs 92% CF DOE $60/MWh; CCUS 1.5 GW coal Carbon Clean 90% capture $30/ton 45Q EPA 111(b).

Cap alloc: 9.5-10% ROE to 2027, PJM Missouri $250M rider, FFO/debt 16-18%. 4.2% yield 5% growth 1.5x coverage, $400M buyback <14x P/E. Debt/EBITDA 3.6x 70% fixed green 4.25%.

Risks: gas $150M/$1/MMBtu, La Nina -10% hydro +20% thermal, HVDC delays 300 MW Siemens, FERC 2222 VPP vs. PURPA QF, IRA 45V SMR NuScale $100M.

Outlook: mid-single EPS compounding, powering tomorrow's grid.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to discuss the financials.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.42 and revenue of $4.75 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $1.3 billion, primarily focused on renewables integration and grid modernization. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Elena. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Tami Gupta with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Tami Gupta: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for further expansion in renewables and storage?

Sarah Kline: Certainly. As I detailed earlier, our 12.5 GW pipeline is progressing well, with key projects like the ERCOT solar-storage hybrids and PJM BESS deployments providing dispatchable clean power. We're scaling to meet data center demand, locking in high-IRR PPAs, and leveraging IRA incentives for cost advantages, all while advancing hydrogen pilots for long-term decarbonization.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

John Lee: What is your outlook for rate base growth and EPS through 2025?

Elena Vasquez: Great question. We're targeting that 6.5-7% CAGR in rate base, supported by our $22 billion five-year capex, with strong regulatory recovery and load growth from electrification. Combined with FY25 EBITDA guidance of $5.2-5.5 billion and EPS $5.80-6.20, this positions us for robust growth, hedged against key risks like inflation and commodity prices.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain disruptions and interconnection delays?

Mike Thompson: Thanks for the question. We've invested upfront in long-term PPAs with suppliers like First Solar and Vestas to lock in efficiencies, contributed $300 million to grid upgrades to accelerate queues, and diversified via JVs for offshore projects. Our early queue strategies and reconductoring pilots minimize delays, ensuring we deliver on our COD timelines.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Sarah Kline for closing remarks.

Sarah Kline: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning EnergiCore Utilities for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in EnergiCore Utilities.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
